Cyberpunk 2077 is a 2020 first person action RPG created by CD projekt Red and based on Cyberpunk, a series of pen and paper roleplaying games created by Michael Pondsmith, a man who is probably tired of saying “I told ya so.” Over the last 35 years.

Set in the fictional city of Night City, a corporate shit hole where everything is run by some sort of conglomerate or another. One of the city states that now exists in the former United States after 77 or so years of endless woopsie poopsies, Night City is the gathering ground of every important entity and person on the planet. Its a place where you can pay EMS to come in literally guns blazing and where kids cartoons tell you to not look people in the eye because they might just attack you like some sort of angry robot baboon. This is the furthest in the Cyberpunk timeline we’ve ever been, with Pondsmith’s RED being an inbetween of Cyberpunk 2020 and this one.

You play as V, a Night City Merc who comes from one of three backgrounds: Street Kid, Nomad, and Corpo. After doing your background intro, you and Jackie, your best friend, go into business of being street Mercs together, solving problems in return for Eurodollars, the dominant currency in Night City because who still pays with USDs? After a series of events, V finds himself with a construct ingrained in his cyberbrain, the construct of Johnny Silverhand, a deceased Terrorist who blew up Arasaka tower back in the distant future of 2023. Now, with Johnny’s consciousness bleeding into yours, and slowly taking over your entire body, you and your headmate set out on a journey to save both of you, or at the very least get Johnny out of your brain.

I really like this one, took me four tries, but this time I stuck with it. Mind you I’m playing this game in 2026, so a good chunk of the problems it had in 2020-2022 or so aren’t present anymore. Problems are still there, I got some bugs every now and then, but it still plays fine for me.

The game is a first person Action RPG with an emphasis on the action, stats and weapons do matter, but it isn’t like a lot of it’s contemporaries where you just shwack someone with a sword that feels like a foam bat to swing or shoot them in the head for 15 minutes until they finally drop. From what I understand, enemies don’t really level with you as much as you get better at killing them. There wasn’t really anywhere I couldn’t go early on and I wasn’t being one shotted, so I figure levels are more about what perks you pick up and how much you put into your six stats.

You can put points into muscle, reflexes, cool, tech, netrunner, and a secret, nefarious sixth option. Stats work up to 20 points, with each milestone point giving you more perks to unlock. Stuff like doing more damage with a sword if you have a sandevastan, you know that thing David had in that anime that made you buy this game? Everyone has one of those now, how time flies.
More points in muscle lets you rip open heavy doors, tech can help you bypass security, Netrunner lets you upload all three shrek movies directly into someone’s brain, etc.

Outside of your stats, there’s also cyberware, which is probably the coolest part of the game. Unlike Adam Jensen, V doesn’t really mind turning himself into a total freak show, with stuff like Gorilla Arms and legs joints that let him run like one of those cute horse girls from that anime I like. Stuff like brain implants that let you upload the Shrek movies faster, an epidermal skin graft that lets you cloak, weird, psycho shit like that.

Looking more into Cyberpunk, there’s an anti-personnel program called Brainwipe that lets you just delete someone’s Id from their cyberbrains and leaves their bodies a drooling caveman. Looking more into it, there’s also a program called Soulkiller where it still does that but also uploads their entire being into a matrix where you can just torture them for all eternity if you want.

I don’t like the Cyberpunk world, it scares me.

Like I said before, combat actually feels nice in this game. Both melee weapons and guns have a nice crunchy oomph to them and people fall apart like you just threw a baseball through a mannequin. Weapons let you shred people to pieces, with their guts and limbs going flying the more ammo you pump into them. Swords will flat out dismember or behead people and I punched a guy so hard with my gorilla arms one time that he bounced off the wall and just kept going into space.
That was probably a glitch but I’m going to pretend V can just do that.

The story is actually keeping me interested. V and Johnny play off one another really well and its just kind of funny that I have a tulpa that rides shotgun with you in your car. Everyone is voice acted pretty well and I don’t think I’ve met anyone that V can talk to on a regular basis that I don’t look.

Night City might be one of my favorite places in a video game at this point as well. Its this mix of modern and futuristic taking a lot of ques from the 2012 Dredd movie. Like, as soon as you leave the industrial and metropolitan area everything just feels like it was forgotten or thrown away by the people at large. On one side you have mega structures with probably thousands of apartments in them, and then on the other side there are literal mountains of garbage bags and thrown away appliances like fridges and flatscreen TVs.

There’s this thing in universe called a Braindance, which is basically this VR headset that lets you go through experiences, either fictional or real, that other people made. You can see people using these throughout the world and its anything from just watching a historical soccer game or playing out an elaborate roleplay fantasy all the way to first person sexual encounters and straight up snuff films.
You’d know what its like to kill someone because it would feel like you’re the one who killed the other guy, or got killed, you basically feel everything the person the shard (Think like an advanced SD card for your brain) came from.

But at the same time, when you go into the slums or the outskirts of town, you can find people in just regular-ass internet cafes or video game cafes. Its like luxury is treated like a hand me down in Night City, where the more affluent can to screw around with advanced technology, but the less fortunate are skill playing COD4 on the 360. Which is probably more true to life than you think.

Also, you can’t use the old internet, its completely swamped by a world ending eldritch super virus being held off by a virtual wall that cuts the new internet off from the old. Gamefaqs is just gone now so all those cool text walkthroughs are lost to time.

Also, yeah, you can pay a heavily armed EMS called Trauma Team to barge into gun fights and come get you guns blazing. Not you in game, but in universe.
Can you imagine just being able to call Nurse Joy with a shotgun for back up?
Night City is very much a good “Drive around” type of video game city. I really like to look at it and rarely use the fast travel unless I’m really in a hurry.

It has its technical issues still. Sometimes the graphics will just wig out, and I doubt this game plays well on anything lower than an 8gb GPU.
Michael Pondsmith is an interesting guy, and he crafted a pretty cool world with his Cyberpunk RPGs. Go check out R. Talsorian games sometimes, the website still looks like it was made in Web 1.0, its kind of fun.

Like the Cyberware you find in Night City, your expectations for this game need to be properly calibrated in order to get the most enjoyment out of it.  What it is not is a deep RPG with an immersive world that changes according to your choices and your actions, nor is it the absolutely buggy mess that it was upon first release.  What it actually is, is an action game with light RPG character progression on top of a large and beautiful albeit kind of shallow open-world.

The gunplay itself is fine, as are the skill trees.  CD Projekt Red has never blown me away with the combat of their Witcher games, and I enjoy it here in Cyberpunk more than any of the three Witcher titles but the game really struggles to make the encounters interesting.  Other than wielding a melee weapon or a ranged weapon, there is little difference between enemies and most encounters are just waves of enemies who may take cover but rarely employ any more tactics than that.

The graphics and art design are undoubtedly the best part of the game, and if you want to play something that justifies the steep price of current graphic cards, Cyberpunk will do that for you.

Phantom Liberty is undoubtedly a step in the right direction, brining more intricate quest lines and more satisfying action set-pieces.  I hope CDPR don't have to spend so much time and resource developing an engine, and can devote more time to making the world reactive and interesting in the sequel.

I was hesitant to buy Cyberpunk 2077 after its disastrous release in 2020. Five years later, after the 2.3 patch and mostly good reviews, I decided to dive in. And I am SO glad I did.

The customisation, characters, skills, hacking, worldbuilding and details, weapons, hacking and vehicles are all excellent. Multiple branching storylines and endings. After 47 hours, I've finished my first playthrough and will be moving straight on to another! That is, after I get over the emotional damage from the ending I got. Truly a remarkable game.

There are still some bugs and graphical/performance issues, but the story and rest of the gameplay let you quickly move on. The game is still being worked on and updated, so these may resolve themselves in the future.

Do yourself a favour and play the game blind, no spoilers. It's worth it.

It is indeed a very story-rich game, and I love how almost everything in it is supported by background lore, even down to small details. This depth makes the world feel alive and meaningful, encouraging players to pay attention and stay engaged with the narrative. The gameplay itself is not particularly difficult, since the game provides a wide range of tools and options to handle different situations. However, the challenging part is managing the dialogue choices, as making the wrong decision can sometimes lead to mission failure, which is never a good outcome.

While some bugs can still be found, they are usually easy to notice and avoid. Overall, the game has clearly improved over the years, showing steady development and refinement that make the experience increasingly enjoyable.

Cyberpunk 2077 immediately stands out for its visuals and storytelling.

Night City looks incredible — dense, atmospheric, and full of detail. The lighting, character models, and overall presentation are top-tier, especially at night. Even just walking or driving around the city feels immersive.

The story hooks you quickly. Dialogue is strong, characters feel grounded, and the world-building pulls you in without needing hours to get interesting.

I haven’t played long enough to judge the full gameplay loop or endgame, but as a first impression, it’s polished, engaging, and easy to get absorbed in.

If the rest of the game holds up like the opening hours, it’s definitely worth your time.

You've been sucked into a game rigged against you that you can never win, and maybe never even truly quit, but you can find some kind of peace and fulfilment in your own small slice of life, and maybe, if you're lucky, never fade away.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a stunning, immersive, emotionally evasive masterpiece that absolutely nails the vibes and then dodges long-term narrative responsibility like a corpo dodges taxes.

As a game? Ridiculously good.
Gunplay? Crunchy.
Build variety? Delicious.
Night City? A neon-drenched “don’t text your ex” mood board that I would absolutely move into despite the gunfire.

Driving through the city at night with the radio on makes you feel like the main character of a movie that ends badly but looks incredible while doing it.

Side quests and character stories? Genuinely fantastic. Some of the most human, grounded writing in modern games. You help people through trauma, grief, identity crises, family disasters. It’s intimate, messy, real.

And then the ending rolls up like:

“Cool emotional growth. Anyway, choose your flavor of existential shrug.”

I really thought all the relationships, gangs, and connections I built would matter more in the final stretch. You spend dozens of hours forming bonds, earning trust, changing lives. You choose a life path, you make dialog choices based on your attributes.

…and the finale goes:

“That’s nice. Please proceed to one of two narrative lanes. No, your friends cannot come.”

Is that thematically consistent with a dystopian hellscape run by megacorps? Yes.
Is it also emotionally unsatisfying? Also yes.

My ending felt:
Not heroic.
Not triumphant.
Not particularly rewarding.
Very lonely.
...yet weirdly, cathartically freeing.

Which, to be fair, is probably the most on-brand outcome possible for this world and narrative.

The game is brilliant at moments. Atmosphere. Character writing. Personal stakes.
It’s just less interested in big-picture emotional payoff where everything you did comes crashing together in the finale. Nothing really does.

So no, the story didn’t rearrange my DNA. It didn’t spiritually supplex me. But it did give me a memorable ride, some genuinely great character arcs, and a beautifully miserable city I’ll think about for a long time.

Would I replay the whole thing again? Probably not. It's a fantastic narrative action game, but a mid-at-best Roleplaying game (yeah, I know CDPR even removed any and all RPG tags from all the marketing).
Do I regret playing it? Not even a little.

Night City is a great ride.
But she really doesn’t care about you or your choices.
Just like your ex.

[h3]TL;DR: Possibly my new favourite game. Absolutely one of the best RPGs I've ever played, and I still have a second play through with the DLC to experience. [u]Must-play[/u] if you dig games by Bethesda, Obsidian, Bioware etc.[/h3]

I've had this in my library for years and tried to pick it up multiple times, but it never hooked me. After watching Edgerunners however, I became a bit obsessed by Cyberpunk's lore and aesthetic, so decided to give it another go. [b]It's all I've played and thought about for the last three weeks[/b].
[list]
[*] Night City is beautiful and alive (even with my wooden PC running it on medium). Every character action has an animation - immersion is incredible. No matter where you go there is something interesting to see or do.
[*] The gunplay is exhilarating, melee combat is dynamic and a lot of fun, and quick hacks are probably my favourite combat/environmental feature. If like me you weren't hooked immediately, try a different playstyle and you WILL be. You can reset your attributes once per save, so play Act 1, make a save point, experiment.
[*] The main story is emotive and brilliantly written (with a lot of narrative choices offered). The voice acting and mocap are phenomenal, and the inclusion of Keanu lends it a lot of legitimacy. The side quests are some of the most fun and memorable I've had the pleasure of playing in an RPG, and I've barely scratched the surface. There's a fair amount of sex/nudity and gore, but it's done in a very tasteful way - the game treats you like an adult.
[*] The driving is a bit meh, but it does its job - literally a vehicle for showcasing the world. I rarely fast travelled.
[*] Are there bugs? Yes. Do they mar the gameplay? No. It's unreasonable to expect a game/piece of software this comprehensive to not have some bugs. I understand that on launch this game was a mess, but I literally only experienced 1 or 2 visual bugs during my first playthrough. Not at all an issue. 
[/list]
I'm only 46 hours in, so I may update my review once I've delved into more side-quests and played through the DLC. However, as someone who loves RPGs, [b]I unapologetically give this game a 10/10.[/b]
Despite hearing countless comments about the rocky start of the game, I still had it saved for a while under things I want to buy. Now, its one of my top and favorite game. I highly recommend!

Just one point. The game difficulty is not really well balanced.
Way too easy on "hard", sometimes too hard on "very hard" but you can change the setting in game.

Story is short, which is okay, but you get to the no return point very fast. The story line is build in a way that rushes you to finish it so you naturally end up leave side quests/missions that impacts ending aside. So you get 30 hours of main story and then you just spent maybe 40-70 hours on side missions, and even more hours if you do all side gigs and scans and then finally you get to do the main last mission. I wished they did the bigger/more important side missions more integrated in the narrative, for example, making them necessary to first complete before progressing story. Aside that, and the exaggerated amount of gigs and scans that ended up being more repetitive than fun after a while, I think it's a really good game.

Don't really care for the haters. Did it release buggy? On Console hell yeah. But it was so good I played through 30 hours on the Xbox one S day one. Unfortunately, this is when graphics cards, PS5 and XBeries were sold out. I stopped when I got a PC and started over 10/10

I can't really understand what people see in this mess of a game. Did patching out the worst release in gaming history make people overlook the terrible state it's in. The game remain bug filled, with vapid gameplay, excess yet awful dialogue, a shallow and dull story, the most limited RPG mechanics I've ever seen.

The story is deeply convoluted despite having almost nothing happening in it, you interact with loads of characters but you barely get to know anything about them except the rare NPC who gives you and entire life story even if you don't really care. Dialogue options are almost always something different to what you say often times fully unrelated. The forced linearity of everything is very grating in an "RPG" where you only real choice is guns or melee. People talk so much it's about 70% of the mission content, so much of the game is sat there listening to boring people saying boring stuff with cringe inducing slang. it peaks in the first act and as consolation it shows you a slideshow of V having fun becoming a criminal (something you skip entirely). The path you choose initially affects only dialogue after you finish the first part, it is useless and the fakest feature the game promises. You see lots of things set up that never go anywhere I mean the SWAT team and the Medics are made out as these huge things you never ever interact with. The world feels dead and empty, a lifeless city you go through to get from mission to mission.

Mechanics are terrible the driving especially, GTA has been out for years and they couldn't just copy it or use some racing game code. it feels pre-2000 quality. The combat is fine nothing special, the hacking is sort of cool but it all feels so generic. Skills are fine I've heard they were a lot better before 2.0 but what would I know that awful game essentially no longer exists.

Almost nothing about this game clicks and it's really sad because people talk about it like gaming jesus. Do not waste money and time supporting this product, it's some of the worst triple A content people praise.

I was admittedly hesitant to start the game after everything I'd heard about launch. After hearing from friends the game was in a much better state I finally gave it a shot. This game blew me away, the story is absolutely phenomenal and I felt like I was really able to immerse myself into the world of Night City. Phantom Liberty was a lot of fun too. Highly recommend anyone check this game out if you're looking for something to invest a lot of time into.

easily my favourite open world game ever made. industry leading graphics, writing and world building. the only thing that stops it being a 10/10 is that CDPR have limited modding capabilities a fair bit and obviously it requires a very high end pc if you want to use path tracing, ray tracing with dlss though is completely fine even on medium builds.

I'm a fan of these types of RPG games, having played Skyrim, every fallout, and a looong list of this genre, and when Cyberpunk came out, it was awful, badly optimized, full of bugs and all that stuff that everybody knows, now 6 years later i can say it is a pretty fixed game, different even in the UI, but i cant say it doesn't have any bugs, there is a lot, but is nothing compared to what it used to be, for me is no problem (i played Starfield and i loved it haha).
I think the biggest sin of Cyberpunk is all the cut content, i mean, i completed the story, gigs and secondary missions in like 80ish hours, and you can feel that in a lot of em there was more which didn't make the cut, which is sad cuz it has a lot of potential.
If u are a lover of RPGs like me and doesnt care too much of bugs, buy it! even tho theres a lot of wasted potential in content, it is a pretty fun game, with a lot of builds, endings, and you can feel that it was made and updated with love, its just the crunch that killed this game release and potential.
